comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics
comparator.sourceNotes: The regulations allocate 135 EC to the major and 45 EC to the optional course profile for students without a dedicated minor. This example uses the first listed context and intermediate macroeconomics choices, one second-year major elective, and the three third-year courses listed for the Economics study route. The flexible study routes can be combined.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest option combines economics, business and empirical methods, covering the Economics interest. The two further options pursue public economics through law, institutions and policy analysis, and finance through banking, markets and quantitative methods. Management remains supported through strategy, organisations, marketing and innovation, with substantial overlap with the closest option. The three-option limit is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Utrecht introduces economic methodology, disciplinary history and academic skills. UCR develops academic skills separately and introduces market models in Introduction to Economics.
Both introduce supply and demand, production and market structure. UCR also uses part of this course for macroeconomics.
Both study choices under uncertainty and strategic interaction. UCR also studies market efficiency, externalities and government intervention.
Both develop macroeconomic reasoning. UCR applies it to open economies, monetary and fiscal policy, and business cycles.
Both study market failure, institutions and policy. UCR emphasises public goods, taxation and welfare.
Utrecht has a separate intermediate course on cycles and international money. UCR treats cycles and open-economy policy within International Macroeconomics.
Utrecht offers a dedicated Labour Economics course. UCR treats labour markets, taxation and welfare within broader economics courses.
Utrecht offers a dedicated Development and Growth course. UCR addresses growth within macroeconomics.
Both introduce firms and strategic decisions. UCR gives added weight to entrepreneurship and business formation.
Matched explicitly after semantic review: Accounting and Finance corresponds to Accounting & Corporate Finance.
Both examine financial decisions. Utrecht focuses on corporate finance, while this UCR course focuses on markets, risk and banking.
Both develop calculus and optimisation. UCR includes differential equations and scientific examples.
UCR combines statistics with broader research design.
Both use economic models and data to test hypotheses. UCR includes regression, instrumental variables and simulation.
Utrecht requires a research elective in this example. UCR studies inequality in public economics and sociology and develops empirical methods separately.
Utrecht studies contemporary economics in historical perspective. UCR adds a separate course in moral philosophy.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Optional course profile: year 2, period 3.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Optional course profile: year 2, period 4.
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: no scheduled UCR course was judged a sufficiently direct counterpart to Optional course profile: year 3.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC course culminating in an individual economics research paper. UCR students can choose independent research.

notes.text: Utrecht combines a fixed economics and business core with flexible electives, a research elective and a required 15 EC thesis. The UCR options combine economics with business and data, public policy and institutions, or quantitative analysis for finance.

Utrecht offers dedicated labour economics, development and inequality research in this example. UCR addresses related questions within macroeconomics, public economics and other courses. The finance option develops tools for analysing markets and banking, with less dedicated finance coursework than Utrecht’s Finance study route.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s degree combines economics, business, mathematics and empirical research. Students build an elective profile and complete an applied economics research course with an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines economics and business with data analysis. Two further options focus on public economics and institutions, or finance and quantitative methods. Utrecht offers a more prescribed economics core and a required economics thesis.

curriculum.limitation: This example keeps 45 EC open for elective choices. It includes selected economics electives and the period 4 thesis.

cellNotes.text: Students without a dedicated minor choose one of two context courses.
Students choose one of two intermediate macroeconomics courses.
This example leaves two elective slots open here to meet the 45 EC profiling requirement.
In this example, the open profile must include at least 15 EC of intermediate study and two advanced courses worth 15 EC in total. Course choices are subject to the overlap rules.
This advanced research elective meets the research requirement separately from the thesis.

For the period 4 thesis, students need 90 EC at the start of the academic year. Before the course they must pass Econometrics, two advanced courses including at least one in economics, and the academic skills reflection report.
